title: Etale local logarithmic lifts of a prescribed scheme morphism
statement:
Let $T,Z$ be locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth] with log structures $(M_T,\alpha_T)$ and $(M_Z,\alpha_Z)$ on their small etale sites, and fix a scheme map $g:T\to Z$. Log structures and their morphisms mean sheaves of commutative monoids over the multiplicative structure sheaf with the unit axiom, and scheme maps with compatible inverse-image monoid-sheaf maps, as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]; neither fineness nor saturation is required. Let $\{q_a:T_a\to T\}_{a\in A}$ be a jointly surjective etale covering [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Equip $T_a$ with $M_T|_{T_a}$, so $q_a$ is strict. Suppose log morphisms $G_a:(T_a,M_T|_{T_a})\to(Z,M_Z)$ have underlying maps $gq_a$ and agree on $T_a\times_TT_b$ [def-pc-fibre-product].

Then there is a unique homomorphism $u:g^{-1}M_Z\to M_T$ satisfying $\alpha_Tu=g^\sharp\circ g^{-1}\alpha_Z$ and restricting to $G_a^\flat$ for every $a$. Equivalently there is a unique log morphism $G=(g,u)$ with prescribed underlying map $g$ inducing all $G_a$. Equality of two log morphisms with underlying map $g$ is detected by these restrictions.

Let in addition $(S,M_S)$ be any locally Noetherian log scheme, let $t:(T,M_T)\to(S,M_S)$ and $z:(Z,M_Z)\to(S,M_S)$ be log morphisms, and suppose their underlying scheme maps satisfy $zg=t$. If $zG_a=tq_a$ as log morphisms for every $a$, then $zG=t$ as log morphisms; the converse also holds. Finally, if $g$ is a scheme isomorphism and every $G_a^\flat:(gq_a)^{-1}M_Z\to M_T|_{T_a}$ is an isomorphism of monoid sheaves, then $G$ is a log isomorphism. Its inverse has underlying map $g^{-1}$ and induces the local inverse monoid-sheaf maps on the cover $\{gq_a:T_a\to Z\}$. These assertions include uniqueness of the inverse and its compatibility with $S$ whenever the relative hypotheses hold.

proof.text: Work in a common larger universe with small site skeletons as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Put $N=g^{-1}M_Z$ and $P=M_T$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. Inverse image preserves finite products and the terminal sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures](1), so applying it to multiplication and the unit equips $N$ with its commutative monoid structure; its axioms are the images of the monoid diagrams. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open], $T_{\mathrm{et}}/T_a$ is the small etale site of $T_a$, with the same coverings. Restriction to this slice is the inverse image along $q_a$: in the inverse-image colimit of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures], at $W\to T_a$ the object $(W\to T,\,W\to W\times_TT_a)$ given by the graph is final in the opposite indexing category. Indeed each pair $(V\to T,\,W\to V\times_TT_a)$ determines exactly its first projection $W\to V$, and hence its unique arrow from this graph object before taking the opposite category. The colimit is consequently $F(W\to T)$; these values already form the restriction sheaf, so sheafification changes nothing. The composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] therefore identifies $N|_{T_a}$ with $(gq_a)^{-1}M_Z$. Its associativity makes the two identifications on a double overlap coincide. Thus the given $G_a^\flat$ are compatible maps $u_a:N|_{T_a}\to P|_{T_a}$.

proof.text: Apply the morphism clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] to the underlying sheaves of sets $N,P$, with $U=T$ the final etale object and cover $\{T_a\to T\}$. The overlap hypothesis is precisely the compatibility of the $u_a$ from step 1. It supplies a unique sheaf map $u:N\to P$ restricting to every $u_a$.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps, as stated in the morphism clause of lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent.

proof.text: For each etale $W\to T$, its pullbacks $W_a=W\times_TT_a$ form a covering. For $x,y\in N(W)$, the sections $u(xy)$ and $u(x)u(y)$ restrict to the same section on every $W_a$, since $u_a$ is multiplicative. The equalizer axiom of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] implies equality on $W$; the same argument with $1$ proves $u(1)=1$. Likewise $\alpha_Tu(x)$ and $g^\sharp(g^{-1}\alpha_Z(x))$ agree after every restriction, since each $G_a$ is a log morphism, hence agree in $\mathcal O_T(W)$. Thus $u$ is a monoid-sheaf homomorphism with the required structure-map equation, and $G=(g,u)$ is a log morphism by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The log structures themselves are given, so no new unit-axiom verification is needed.

source.place: VI 1.1, printed p.69; expansion using the equalizer sheaf axiom (Stacks Tag 00VM, definition-sheaf-sets).

proof.text: If two log morphisms over the prescribed scheme map $g$ induce the same local morphisms, their underlying maps of set sheaves $N\to P$ are both amalgamations of the same family. The uniqueness clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] makes them equal. A log morphism consists exactly of its scheme map and its compatible monoid-sheaf map, so this proves both uniqueness of $G$ and detection of equality by restriction.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps, uniqueness; ILO VI 1.1 for log morphisms.

proof.text: Under the relative hypotheses, $zG$ and $t$ have the same scheme map $zg=t$. Their monoid maps, with the source identified using [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], are $u\circ g^{-1}(z^\flat)$ and $t^\flat:t^{-1}M_S\to M_T$. Associativity of that comparison identifies their restrictions with $(zG_a)^\flat$ and $(tq_a)^\flat$. These agree by assumption, so uniqueness in [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] makes the two global maps equal. Conversely restricting $zG=t$ gives $zG_a=tq_a$.

Now suppose $g$ is a scheme isomorphism and each $u_a$ is an isomorphism. Its inverses $v_a:P|_{T_a}\to N|_{T_a}$ agree on double overlaps: they are inverses of the same restricted map there, and an inverse is unique. Apply [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] to obtain $v:P\to N$. Sectionwise separatedness as in step 3 proves that $v$ preserves multiplication and $1$. The maps $vu,\mathrm{id}_N$ have identical restrictions, as do $uv,\mathrm{id}_P$, so the same gluing uniqueness gives $vu=\mathrm{id}_N$ and $uv=\mathrm{id}_P$. Composing the equation of step 3 with $v$ gives $\alpha_T=g^\sharp\circ g^{-1}\alpha_Z\circ v$.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps, applied to the inverse maps and their composite equations; Tag 00VM, definition-sheaf-sets.

proof.text: Write $h=g^{-1}:Z\to T$. Because $g,h$ are inverse scheme maps, composition with them gives inverse equivalences of the small etale sites: $(W\to T)\mapsto(W\to T\xrightarrow{g}Z)$ and its reverse, preserving coverings. Under these equivalences the map $v:M_T\to g^{-1}M_Z$ is exactly a monoid-sheaf map $w:h^{-1}M_T\to M_Z$. The structure-sheaf map $g^\sharp$ is invertible under the same equivalence; thus the last equation of step 6 becomes $\alpha_Zw=h^\sharp\circ h^{-1}\alpha_T$. Hence $H=(h,w)$ is a log morphism by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The equations $vu=1$ and $uv=1$ give $HG=1_T$ and $GH=1_Z$, respectively. On the covering $\{gq_a:T_a\to Z\}$, $w$ is the transported $v_a$, exactly the stated local inverse monoid-sheaf map. Any two inverses agree since $H=H(GH\prime)=(HG)H\prime=H\prime$. Finally, if $zG=t$, then $tH=zGH=z$, so the inverse is also over $S$.
